summary:
# NOTES ON THE THREE BOOKS (compact reference)

## BOOK 1 of 3: "Shoulder to Shoulder" by Gordon Stables (Gutenberg 76046)

**Frame:** Narrator (Dr. Gordon Stables, "Williamie") recalls grandfather "Auld-da" (Ian/John Robertson, later Sergeant, then Colour-Sergeant, Royal Scots/1st Royals) telling stories by the fire. Auld-da died aged 89. Narrator is "I"; Auld-da's soldier life is told in chapters. Motto: "Be Britain still to Britain true" (Burns). Epigraph: Sir John Moore "Hurrah, my lads; remember Egypt!"

**Book I – In the Highlands a Hundred Years Ago**
- Ch I: Auld-da's cottage, peat fire, creepie (stool). Narrator a small boy, Auld-da's favourite. Codlin apple tree; quarter-day trips to Aberdeen for half-pay; half-crowns. Auld-da wore away "in his 89th year"; last words "Don't I know my own laddie! Mercy! Mercy!" Buried beside Bass o' Ury.
- Ch II: Narrator a Jacobite at seven; mother sang Jacobite songs ("He's owre the hills", "Cam' ye by Athol", "O wae's me for Prince Charlie"). Cumberland ("bloody Duke") shot a wounded Highlander at Culloden; officer refused ("I am your humble servant, but not your executioner"). Auld-da: "Your father's kin were rebels… your mother's forbears, the Robertsons of the Braes of R----, were royalists." Auld-da's regiment: 1st Royal Scots, "Pontius Pilate's Guards"; Duke of Kent was colonel; Duke of Kent = Queen's father; "her father was the means of saving my life."
- Ch III: Family history: great-grandfather (d. aged 101, found dead against pine, snuff-box). Fiona Stuart (18, dark-brown eyes, "Gipsy") sister-in-law of Robertson; Lord Lovat's castle Belladrum. Raoul McIvor "Raoul Dhu"/Black Ronald, musician, wild. Raoul shot a hare; Fiona's heart belongs to Ian Robertson, Royal Scots officer ("ma ghaol ma chree"). Raoul seized her arm; dwarf Muirachie (faithful, broken English, "ta leddies") strangled Raoul from behind; "When ta dew falls ta rascal Raoul Dhu no pe deaded."
- Ch IV: Fontenoy (1745; Saxe; Cumberland; Dutch cowardice; Irish regiment). Robertson refuses Stuart standard; Raoul threatens. Muirachie spies. Raoul with rebels after Culloden, plans revenge. Robertson hides family in whisky-still cave ("Corney's Cave"-type); Fiona (Mary's sister) disguised in Tam-o'-Shanter/plaid runs ~14 miles to Duke's camp near Culloden; wounded soldier given water in her bonnet; rebel spy chase; sentry; Captain McDonald; Ian (officer) is her lover. "To horse! To horse!" 33 horsemen.
- Ch V: Attack on farm: Raoul leads ~50 rebels; torches; axes; fire in copse; Muirachie rescues women from cave; battering-ram; hand-to-hand. "The red-coats are coming!" Ian vs Raoul; Raoul pierced; Fiona stops Ian killing him; Raoul later executed in Edinburgh. Muirachie died saving cattle. Auld-da born on the Braes higher up.

**Ch VI–VII (school):** Narrator's walk; Miss Steelyard ("I hate boys"; "monkey"); Auld-da (Ian) at Freeschal's school (dominie Freeschal); tawse; Gaelic forbidden Fridays; "Sir John Robertson" joke. Dominie's wife Mrs. Freeschal; daughter Rachel (age 8, fair hair, blue eyes). Pupil Tonal (Touvil, later pipe-major); Mrs. Nairn (Johnnie Nairn's mother with broom); Tom Grahame (big, bully); "Preen Mhor" (big pin) nickname. Ian shut in school, climbs chimney, stuck, slid down, frightens dominie (owl cry; dominie faints; hat kicked).

**Ch VIII–IX:** Conspiracy: Tonal and Ian burn the tawse in forest; Tonal enlists. Cock-fight; Ian king of school; Reel of Tulloch with Rachel; Tom Grahame threatens; Tom/Ian fight, kilt pin wounds Tom; Ian nurses Tom. Dominie leaves; Ian leaves home at 15 for Inverness (staymaker Mr Craig, rats). Cousin Fraser (Falkirk Lodge; Captain Fraser of Black Watch); shilling taken; Ian rejects service "I am a Robertson and a loyalist." Collie Dash.

**Ch X–XI:** Ian throws King's shilling into sea. Old fisherman and daughter (buxom lass) feed him. Outlaw in Corney's Cave (heather bed). Rachel's note and four-bladed clover ("trust more in God than even the four-bladed clover"). Soldiers arrest him at dominie's; girl Ellen (Beauly inn) helps escape by blacking sergeant's men's faces. Lawyer John Chisholm of Inverness; recruited at Fort George by sergeant ("We'll call you John"). Enlisted as Private John Robertson, 1st Royals.

**Book II – Off to join his regiment**
- Ch I: drill; Sergeant Brown; Captain Drake (fist, "I never lose mine at all"); McGruer vs Pope/Playfair fight. Ship packet Vengeful to Leith.
- Ch II: storm; cattle thrown overboard; Edinburgh.
- Ch III: Edinburgh Castle; Dr McLeod (giant surgeon, "Doctor McLeod"); hornpipe on dinner table (wager). Duel: Lt Blood (little, wears stays) vs McLeod, thrown through window; O'Reilly vs Drake duel (Jones, Blood shot); Blood's busk saved him.
- Ch IV: Captain Drake's account of French Revolution, Toulon, Danton, Robespierre.
- Ch V: Toulon, Corsica (Bastia, Calvi). Drake captured by brigands (hag, stripped, returned via Dr. McLeod/O'Reilly). Morello storming.
- Ch VI: John made corporal, then sergeant. Freemason; drunk on road; Colonel W—'s servant; colonel forgives.
- Ch VII: Napoleon; Irish rebellion; Dr McNiven; Humbert; Bay of Hague flotilla.
- Ch VIII: Furlough 1801; Craig dead; Ellen; Rachel dead; Aboukir/Alexandria 21 Mar 1801; Drake shot in leg/fell; Tom Grahame in 42nd; Captain Fraser dies in Ian's arms (letter for daughter Ailie).

**Book III – From War to Gentle Peace**
- Ch I: Duke of Kent at Ramsgate; flea anecdote; flogging; Tonal the piper; "Miller o' Drone" at church.
- Ch II: Gibraltar; Duke's reforms; vendetta; stabbing of John.
- Ch III: Mutiny; murder of Mr. Myers box; meeting at Mr Milan's; oath; Christmas Eve mutiny.
- Ch IV: dying soldier forgives Duke; 26 Dec second mutiny; Reilly shot; Napoleon's Enghien murder; Nelson's brig.
- Ch V: Trafalgar; Drake's recruiting; meets Eleanor (Ellen) Stapleton at Booterstown.
- Ch VI: Dundalk fair; St Patrick schooner; Copenhagen; marriage to Ellen.
- Ch VII: Peninsula; Wellesley; Moore's retreat; Tom Grahame's adopted Annie.
- Ch VIII–IX: Corunna; Moore dies; Tonal marries Spanish girl and gets bagpipes.
- Ch X: Ellen follows; Bergen-op-Zoom; Ellen shoots harpy (cannonball in stocking); son Robert born on battlefield.
- Ch XI: Atlantic; shipwreck Anticosti; Canada war; Chippewa.
- Ch XII–XIII: Red-Eye (Micmac); Mary (narrator's mother) taken by Micmacs; Tonal captured; Red-Eye dies saving Mary; "Child of my heart."
- Ch XIV: Battle; Red-Eye buried; Waterloo missed; Napoleon at St Helena.

## BOOK 2 of 3: "Willow the King" by J. C. Snaith (Gutenberg 73075)

**Cast:** Narrator (I; cricketer, billiard-room host, batsman). Little Clumpton Cricket Club vs Hickory. Team members: Optimist (Brightside), Pessimist (Grimston), Humourist (Merryweather, "Jessop"), Worry (Daunton, the pro is named "Daunton"), Treasurer, Captain (Halliday, H.J.), Secretary (Lawson), General Nuisance (Hon. John Blenkinsop-Comfort), Ancient (J.F.S. Oldknow), Lennox, Merryweather. William = narrator's manservant; Wiggles = ground-man; Mrs. Jennings; Dimsdale = narrator (R. C. Richard Cranford Dimsdale). Trentham family (Rectory): Rev. George Trentham (Rector, D.D.); Laura Mary "Grace" Trentham (twin, heroine, brown holland, Zingari tie); T.S.M. "Tommy" (Harrow captain); H.C. (Charlie, best bowler, "Charlie"); A.H. "Archie" Trentham (= A.E. Stoddart); Captain George (Artillery, ex-Gloucestershire captain, "old George"); Rev. E.J.H. Elphinstone "Toddles" (curate, little parson); Carteret (fat barrister, short-slip); Biffin (umpire/ old pro); Jane (maid); Augustus (butler); Jennings (butler); Earl Boughey ("Dick"). Baron? none. Stoddart going to Australia.

**Events in order:**
1. Eve of Little Clumpton v. Hickory; Captain's pipe; Secretary; General Nuisance announces Trenthams coming, Charlie's mother-in-law ill.
2. William (valet) loses Authentic cap; narrator reads Sportsman; General Nuisance delivers paper; news of Billy drunk; cap sent for from Thornhill.
3. Ground: Miss Grace in brown holland drives coach; criticises wicket; Grace bowls to A.H. at nets; Hickory coach.
4. Toss confusion: both sides claim to have won toss, coin re-tossed; Little Clumpton bats first; narrator out LBW to Tommy's (T.S.M.'s) ball for 7; Halliday 98 not out at lunch; Oldknow 46.
5. Lunch in Grace's coach; champagne; toast to Stoddy; Charlie's Stoddy-omission joke; dream of wire "Name inadvertently omitted."
6. Record: Halliday 204, partnership 301; Little Clumpton 518/4 declared-like at 5pm; Oldknow 101; Grimston 86; Merryweather 28; Blenkinsop-Comfort 59.
7. Night: narrator in love; General Nuisance mocks; sister Mary; Grace at Rectory single-wicket matches; Gloucester v Middlesex county match: narrator joins as Gloucester side, Grace captain; W.G. (Grace) jokes; library window broken by Archie; Rectory rules; cucumbers; oath on hat; Biffin umpire.
8. Tea; Rector's tobacco plants; Harrow boy Tom selected for Kent (A.J. = Webbe telegram); Grace replies; Stoddart telegram: "If Hawke wants you for India, sing slow. You are going with me. Stoddart."
9. Narrator's proposal in library while Grace scores averages ("Dimmy"); she refuses until telegram; challenges single wicket on lawn Monday.
10. Next morning: Dimsdale practises bowling with Grace; Rectory single wicket; narrator bats first, scores 23 (dropped by Cheery), out; Grace declares by knocking own wicket with bat; narrator's sum; Biffin "Hout, fair hout."
11. Epilogue: Morning Post marriage notice: Richard Cranford Dimsdale to Laura Mary ("Grace") Trentham, 11th inst., Hickory parish church.

Also ad (Guy Boothby; Lt. Shaw etc.) appended.

## BOOK 3 of 3: "A Dead Reckoning" by T. W. Speight (Gutenberg 57737)

**Cast:** Clara Brooke (née Danby? no—Clara Danby, narrator heroine, married Gerald). Gerald Brooke (owner of Beechley Towers, Polish-raised, pistol-shooter, six-thousand-a-year). Miss Jane Primby (aunt of Clara). Lady Fanny "Fan" Dwyer (husband Algy Dwyer, yachtsman, Cairo). Baron Otto von Rosenberg (Beaulieu, ex-diplomat, shot dead). George Crofton (cousin of Gerald; Clara's former suitor; gash in upper lip, black eyes). Stephanie Lagrange (circus rider; later Mrs. Crofton; daughter of Jules Picot). Henri Picot (boy, mountebank's son, blue eyes, golden curls). Jules Picot (mountebank, Pandean pipes, drum; murdered Baron von Rosenberg because Von Rosenberg seduced/abandoned daughter Stephanie). Paul Karovsky (Russian, Secret Society; Tribunal; ordered Gerald to kill Von Rosenberg, threatened Clara's widowhood). Bunce (butler). Dixon (groom). Margery Shook (orphan barge girl, witch-like laugh, devoted to Clara, "Muster Geril"). Tom Starkie (friend; father Sir John Starkie, JP, Penrhyn Court). Superintendent J. Drumley (police). Sergeant (Tomlinson, Simcox). Roger Chamfrey (friend, gave Gerald keeper post). Timley (head keeper, cottage; wife). Lucas (mate). James Maynard (= Gerald's alias at Cinder Pit Junction). Slinkey and "Lardy Bill" (gang). Colonel Crofton (fake uncle, actually Lardy Bill). Mr. Sturgess (jeweller). Mrs. Purvis (landlady at Beechley Arms). Euphrosyne Smith (circus friend).

**Events in order:**
1. 24 April (six months married). Clara, Aunt Jane, Lady Fan at Beechley Towers, 14 miles from London. Pistol-practice by Gerald and Baron. Picot and Henri appear with mountebank tricks; Henri given cakes; Bunce rebukes them. Henri "no sister" remark later.
2. Gerald and Baron; Baron borrows the gold-and-silver inlaid Indian pistol (gift from a Nawab). George Crofton visits; quarrels; crushes Gerald's miniature (ground underfoot).
3. Karovsky visits; reveals Gerald's oath of 8 years ago in Warsaw; Tribunal drew lots: Gerald must kill Von Rosenberg (who betrayed a Polish printing press; Karovsky's brother died in mines). Gerald refuses; Karovsky: "Remember!"
4. Ten weeks later: Gerald drafts warning letter to Baron, is interrupted by Clara ("Baron von Rosenberg is dead—murdered"); Dixon's account. Margery reports police; Mr. Tom Starkie warns; Drumley arrives with warrant; Clara lies; Gerald hides in the suit-of-armour alcove (helmet/visor) at the foot of the staircase.
5. Gerald flees to Penrhyn Court (Priest's Hole). Then to Yorkshire moor as "Davis" under Timley; Crofton tracks him; Gerald as Maynard signalman at Cinder Pit Junction.
6. London: Picot's room; Pymm's Buildings (No. 5, Soho) as "Mr & Mrs Stewart." Karovsky appears and offers to take Gerald's place; Picot hides Gerald; Crofton arrives and is bound by Picot with handkerchief gag; Margery; Crofton escapes by burning ropes on lamp.
7. Crofton-Stephanie quarrel at Linden Villa; plan to rob Mr Sturgess's jewels (Lord Leamington's box, 14 April). Stephanie learns Picot is her father.
8. Gang rob attempt at Cinder Pit Junction: Clara and Margery overhear; Margery fixes fog-signals; gang; Lardy Bill (sham parson) binds Gerald; Crofton shoots Gerald in arm; Crofton denounces him; Sergeant Greenholme police arrest gang.
9. Magistrates at Cummerhays: Picot confesses killing Von Rosenberg (Stephanie fled Von Rosenberg, he wouldn't marry; Marie died; Henri). Clara faints. Picot dies in cell by poison in shoe-heel phial; letter to "Madame Brouke"; Henri died in January after an accident.
10. Crofton fake-uncle visit (Lardy Bill); Crofton escapes jail by file/wall. Stephanie reads paper in Cummerhays inn; learns father's identity; she had written to father, letter never arrived.
11. Epilogue (6 weeks later): Gerald and Clara return to Towers. Lady Fan, Tom Starkie, Miss Primby, Margery in new French kid shoes. Crofton shoots at Gerald from terrace window; a dark cloaked figure (Karovsky) knocks gun aside with knife; Crofton dies ("Gerald Brooke, you have won the game!"). Karovsky: "The sentence has been carried into effect... you are absolved." THE END.
